section: Right to Freedom - Article 19 (six freedoms) and reasonable restrictions
subsections: Article 19(1) clauses (a) to (g), deleted clause (f), freedoms not listed, Articles 19-22
Freedom of speech - implied rights recognised by courts
Article 19 availability - citizens only, foreigners, detained persons

accepted.s: How many freedoms are presently guaranteed under Article 19(1) of the Constitution of India?
accepted.x: Article 19(1) presently guarantees six freedoms. Originally, it contained seven freedoms, but the freedom relating to property was deleted.
accepted.tq: Use the numerical change from seven original freedoms to six present freedoms.
accepted.sec: Article 19(1) clauses (a) to (g), deleted clause (f), freedoms not listed, Articles 19-22  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with the corresponding provision of Article 19(1)?
o: Clause (e) — Freedom of speech and expression
Clause (c) — Freedom to move freely throughout India
Clause (b) — Freedom to form associations or unions
Clause (d) — Freedom to move freely throughout India
accepted.x: Article 19(1)(d) guarantees the freedom to move freely throughout the territory of India. Clause (b) concerns peaceful assembly, clause (c) concerns associations, and clause (e) concerns residence and settlement.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between neighbouring Article 19 clauses by matching each clause with its exact freedom.
accepted.sec: Article 19(1) clauses (a) to (g), deleted clause (f), freedoms not listed, Articles 19-22  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The freedom to reside and settle in any part of India is guaranteed under:
accepted.x: Article 19(1)(e) guarantees citizens the freedom to reside and settle in any part of India.
accepted.tq: Test the exact clause number attached to a specific freedom.
accepted.sec: Article 19(1) clauses (a) to (g), deleted clause (f), freedoms not listed, Articles 19-22  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following freedoms is guaranteed under Article 19(1)(g)?
o: Freedom to assemble peaceably and without arms
Freedom to reside and settle in any part of India
Freedom to practise any profession or carry on any occupation, trade or business
accepted.x: Article 19(1)(g) guarantees the freedom to practise any profession or to carry on any occupation, trade or business.
accepted.tq: Match the occupational freedom with its precise constitutional clause.
accepted.sec: Article 19(1) clauses (a) to (g), deleted clause (f), freedoms not listed, Articles 19-22  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Article 19(1)(c):
1. It includes the right to form associations or unions.
2. The reference to co-operative societies was added by the 97th Constitutional Amendment.
3. It originally included the right to acquire, hold and dispose of property.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The right to acquire, hold and dispose of property belonged to Article 19(1)(f), not Article 19(1)(c), and was later deleted.
accepted.tq: Separate the original property clause from the association clause and identify the amendment-added phrase.
accepted.sec: Article 19(1) clauses (a) to (g), deleted clause (f), freedoms not listed, Articles 19-22  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The freedom to acquire, hold and dispose of property was deleted from Article 19(1) by the:
accepted.x: The 44th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1978 deleted Article 19(1)(f), which had guaranteed the freedom to acquire, hold and dispose of property.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the amendment that deleted the property freedom from other major constitutional amendments.
accepted.sec: Article 19(1) clauses (a) to (g), deleted clause (f), freedoms not listed, Articles 19-22  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT included among the six freedoms presently guaranteed by Article 19(1)?
o: Freedom to carry on any occupation, trade or business
Freedom to move freely throughout India
Freedom to acquire, hold and dispose of property
accepted.x: The freedom to acquire, hold and dispose of property was Article 19(1)(f), but it was deleted by the 44th Amendment in 1978. The other three are among the six present freedoms.
accepted.tq: Find the deleted clause rather than selecting one of the six surviving freedoms.
accepted.sec: Article 19(1) clauses (a) to (g), deleted clause (f), freedoms not listed, Articles 19-22  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The group of Fundamental Rights known as the Right to Freedom is contained in:
accepted.x: The Right to Freedom comprises Articles 19 to 22 of the Constitution.
accepted.tq: Identify the constitutional range associated with a named group of Fundamental Rights.
accepted.sec: Article 19(1) clauses (a) to (g), deleted clause (f), freedoms not listed, Articles 19-22  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Freedom of expression under Article 19(1)(a) came into force on:
accepted.x: The freedom of expression under Article 19(1)(a) was in force from 26 January 1950, when the Constitution commenced.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the Constitution’s adoption date from its commencement date.
accepted.sec: Article 19(1) clauses (a) to (g), deleted clause (f), freedoms not listed, Articles 19-22  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following is not expressly enumerated in Article 19(1), but has been recognised by judicial interpretation as part of freedom of speech and expression?
o: Right to acquire property under Article 19(1)(f)
Right to strike as a Fundamental Right
Freedom to travel abroad under Article 19(1)(d)
accepted.x: Freedom of the press is not separately listed in Article 19(1), but courts have read it into freedom of speech and expression. There is no Fundamental Right to strike, travel abroad is associated with Article 21, and Article 19(1)(f) has been deleted.
accepted.tq: Separate judicially implied freedoms from rights expressly listed or specifically excluded.
accepted.sec: Article 19(1) clauses (a) to (g), deleted clause (f), freedoms not listed, Articles 19-22  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
accepted.x: The right to information has been read into Article 19(1)(a). Travel abroad is associated with Article 21, the right to strike is not a Fundamental Right, and clause (f) relating to property has been deleted.
accepted.tq: Distinguish implied rights from rights placed under another Article or not recognised as Fundamental Rights.
accepted.sec: Article 19(1) clauses (a) to (g), deleted clause (f), freedoms not listed, Articles 19-22  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The right to protest has been read into the freedom of speech and expression.
2. The right to strike is a Fundamental Right under Article 19(1)(b).
3. Travel abroad is protected under Article 21 and not under Article 19(1)(d).
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. The right to strike is not a Fundamental Right under Article 19(1)(b), although peaceful protest is protected within constitutional limits.
accepted.tq: Use the false-right trap by distinguishing protest from strike and domestic movement from foreign travel.
accepted.sec: Article 19(1) clauses (a) to (g), deleted clause (f), freedoms not listed, Articles 19-22  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Arrange the following events relating to freedom of speech and expression in chronological order:
A. Decision in Sakal Papers
B. Decision in Romesh Thappar
C. Decision in State of Uttar Pradesh v. Raj Narain
D. Decision in Naveen Jindal
accepted.x: Romesh Thappar was decided in 1950, Sakal Papers in 1962, State of Uttar Pradesh v. Raj Narain in 1975, and Naveen Jindal in 2004.
accepted.tq: Arrange judicial decisions by their stated years, beginning with the earliest case.
accepted.sec: Freedom of speech - implied rights recognised by courts  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which case is associated with the judicial recognition of the right to silence, including the right not to sing the national anthem?
o: Bijoe Emmanuel v. State of Kerala
Anuradha Bhasin v. Union of India
Cricket Association of Bengal v. Union of India
accepted.x: Bijoe Emmanuel (1986) recognised the right to silence, including protection for those who respectfully declined to sing the national anthem.
accepted.tq: Match the implied freedom with the distinctive case fact associated with it.
accepted.sec: Freedom of speech - implied rights recognised by courts  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The right to fly the national flag as an aspect of freedom of expression was recognised in:
accepted.x: The Supreme Court recognised the right to fly the national flag in Naveen Jindal (2004) as an aspect of freedom of expression.
accepted.tq: Use a distinctive judicially implied right to identify the correct case.
accepted.sec: Freedom of speech - implied rights recognised by courts  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Commercial speech, including advertisements, was recognised as part of freedom of speech and expression in:
accepted.x: The Tata Press decision of 1995 recognised commercial speech, including advertisements, as protected expression under Article 19(1)(a).
accepted.tq: Link a specialised form of speech with the case that recognised it.
accepted.sec: Freedom of speech - implied rights recognised by courts  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which case recognised speech over the Internet as an aspect of freedom of speech and expression?
accepted.x: Anuradha Bhasin (2020) recognised that freedom of speech and expression extends to speech over the Internet.
accepted.tq: Use the medium-specific clue to identify the relevant recent constitutional decision.
accepted.sec: Freedom of speech - implied rights recognised by courts  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding judicially recognised aspects of Article 19(1)(a):
1. PUCL litigation is associated with safeguards against phone tapping.
2. Cricket Association of Bengal is associated with telecast and the absence of a government monopoly over airwaves.
3. The freedom to demonstrate or picket necessarily includes a Fundamental Right to strike.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The freedom to demonstrate or picket does not include a Fundamental Right to strike, so statement 3 is false.
accepted.tq: Find the overbroad conclusion in a statement that converts a limited protest right into a right to strike.
accepted.sec: Freedom of speech - implied rights recognised by courts  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following statements best describes the protection of speech under Article 19?
o: It protects only oral speech made in public places.
It is confined to printed newspapers and books.
It applies only when the communication is not commercial.
It protects speech irrespective of the medium through which it is communicated.
accepted.x: Article 19 protects speech and expression irrespective of the medium of communication. Judicial interpretation has extended it to media such as the press, television and the Internet, subject to lawful restrictions.
accepted.tq: Apply the broad constitutional principle to different forms of communication rather than limiting it to print.
accepted.sec: Freedom of speech - implied rights recognised by courts  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which statement correctly distinguishes films from the press in relation to freedom of speech and expression?
o: Films have no protection under Article 19(1)(a), whereas the press has absolute protection.
Films can be pre-censored in a manner in which the press cannot be pre-censored, partly because films reach larger audiences.
The press can always be pre-censored, whereas films can never be pre-censored.
Neither films nor the press can ever be subject to pre-censorship.
accepted.x: Films may be subjected to pre-censorship in a manner in which the press cannot, because films are considered capable of reaching larger audiences. Neither form of expression enjoys absolute protection.
accepted.tq: Test the reversed-comparison trap by distinguishing the treatment of films and the press.
accepted.sec: Freedom of speech - implied rights recognised by courts  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
With reference to Article 19, consider the following statements:
1. Its freedoms are available only to citizens.
2. Foreigners can claim the freedoms under Article 19 in the same manner as citizens.
3. Companies as legal persons cannot themselves claim Article 19 freedoms, although citizen shareholders may sue in appropriate circumstances.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Article 19 rights are available only to citizens; foreigners cannot claim them, and a company as a legal person cannot itself claim them, though citizen shareholders may bring a challenge in appropriate circumstances.
accepted.tq: Distinguish citizens, foreigners and legal persons by identifying the category excluded from Article 19.
accepted.sec: Article 19 availability - citizens only, foreigners, detained persons  [APPSC]

accepted.s: A restriction imposed by a private individual on another person's speech, without any State action, would ordinarily be challenged through:
o: A claim under Article 19(1)(f), which remains enforceable against private persons
An automatic claim under Article 19 against the private individual
An ordinary legal remedy under the applicable law
A claim that Article 19 binds all private persons directly
accepted.x: Article 19 primarily protects citizens against State action. A violation by a private person ordinarily requires an ordinary legal remedy under the applicable law, rather than a direct Article 19 claim against that individual.
accepted.tq: Ask who is bound by the constitutional right before selecting the available remedy.
accepted.sec: Article 19 availability - citizens only, foreigners, detained persons  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements regarding a person who is imprisoned or detained is correct?
o: Detention extinguishes every freedom guaranteed by Article 19.
Detention automatically converts Article 19 rights into property rights.
A detained person retains freedom to move throughout India but loses freedom of expression.
A detained person retains freedom of expression, subject to lawful restrictions, even though movement is curtailed.
accepted.x: Imprisonment or detention curtails movement but does not by itself extinguish freedom of expression. A detained person may, subject to lawful restrictions, write or publish material such as books.
accepted.tq: Separate the specific liberty lost through detention from other freedoms that are not automatically extinguished.
accepted.sec: Article 19 availability - citizens only, foreigners, detained persons  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following statements regarding the voters' right to know is correct?
o: It is unrelated to Article 19(1)(a) because voting is not a form of expression.
It includes the voters' right to know about candidates and is linked with Article 19(1)(a).
It is available only to foreign residents of India.
It was created by deleting Article 19(1)(f).
accepted.x: The voters' right to know about candidates has been treated as an aspect of freedom of speech and expression under Article 19(1)(a). The related material also includes NOTA and ballot secrecy.
accepted.tq: Recognise the information-based aspect of electoral participation as an implied expression right.
accepted.sec: Freedom of speech - implied rights recognised by courts  [APPSC]
